animal_sacred_grove.title: Sacred Grove
animal_sacred_grove.text: Yaksha-marked trees and colored ropes wound around ancient root systems indicate the boundaries of this place. The grove has been tended so long it breathes on its own — the leaves move when nothing else does. Yaksha and Yakshini commune with followers here in the old way: no temples, no intermediaries, just the practitioners and the inhabited earth beneath their feet.

choices.text: Approach the practitioners

outcome.text: A Yakshini turns and regards you without surprise. Earth magic has a price — she names it.

choices.text: Leave them to their work

outcome.text: You walk on. The light here filters differently than the rest of the forest — warmer, somehow, as though the sun is paying attention.

animal_temple_of_the_naga.title: Temple of the Naga
animal_temple_of_the_naga.text: Offerings of saffron-milk and wild flowers line the path to the shrine — fresh, which means someone was here recently. The naga temple here is older than the settlements that surround it, and the naga who receive worship here are older still. Their presence is felt as a weight in the air, like the moment before rain.

choices.text: Ask about their teachings

outcome.text: A practitioner rises smoothly and names the spells they can teach. The price is gold. The naga do not haggle.

choices.text: Move on without disturbing the offerings

outcome.text: You don't touch the flowers. The scent of saffron and something older follows you for a while.

animal_garuda_roost.title: Garuda Roost
animal_garuda_roost.text: A horned pole rises from the high ground — above the canopy where it can be seen from the air, or from a cliff edge visible to anything that flies. The garudas pass through this realm regularly on their circuits between worlds. Followers of all species gather here to wait, to offer, and sometimes to receive teachings when the great birds land. Shyena and kapota are among the most devoted.

choices.text: Speak to the worshippers

outcome.text: One of the worshippers looks up. They teach Air magic here. The price is negotiable, but only within reason.

choices.text: Leave an offering and go

outcome.text: You set something at the base of the pole and move on. The ribbons flutter.

animal_hidden_gompa.title: Hidden Gompa
animal_hidden_gompa.text: A structure of woven branches and packed earth, half-reclaimed by the forest. Inside, mantric syllables are audible — not quite human in their cadence, adjusted over years of practice to harmonize with birdsong and the sounds of the forest. Monks who withdrew from the human realm into the animal realm for solitude. They have been here a long time. The animals have grown accustomed to them.

choices.text: Knock and ask to enter

outcome.text: After a pause, the door opens. A monk gestures you inside. Space magic. What do you need?

choices.text: Don't disturb them

outcome.text: You walk past quietly. The mantras continue without interruption.

animal_medicinal_garden.title: Medicinal Garden
animal_medicinal_garden.text: A clearing carved from the forest floor, every inch cultivated with medicinal plants. Some healers here were born in these forests; others retreated from human settlements to practice more freely. The knowledge is older than any of them — root-knowledge, bark-knowledge, the deep grammar of the healing forest. The teachers share it openly, for a fee.

choices.text: Ask to learn

outcome.text: A healer looks up from her work and nods. She names her price without ceremony.

choices.text: Leave them to their work

outcome.text: You leave without disturbing them. The scent of growing things follows you for some time.

animal_black_lodge.title: Black Lodge
animal_black_lodge.text: The entrance is low, partially hidden by undergrowth. You would miss it if you were not looking. Inside: incense so thick it stings, a khatvanga propped against the wall streaming black ribbons. The practitioner here works alone, without students, without oversight — the animal realm affords the privacy that the human realm did not. They turn when you enter, without surprise.

choices.text: Ask to learn

outcome.text: A hand gestures to a list scratched into the bark of the wall. Spells. Prices. No preamble.

choices.text: Back out

outcome.text: You step back into the daylight. The khatvanga watches you leave.

animal_yogini_circle.title: Circle of the Yoginis
animal_yogini_circle.text: A ring of standing stones in a forest clearing or on a meadow hill — no ceiling, built that way intentionally so the witches can land when they fly in from the sky. The sixty-four forms are inscribed on the inner face of each stone in a script that predates the current tradition of inscription. Practitioners who come here have traveled a long way to reach this circle.

choices.text: Enter the circle

outcome.text: One of the practitioners turns and gestures. No words needed.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You back away slowly. The air around the circle hums for a long time after.

animal_mirror_lake.title: Mirror Lake
animal_mirror_lake.text: A lake so still it seems to reflect a different sky — no wind reaches it, or the water ignores the wind. Enchantment practitioners gather at the shore to meditate on appearance and reality. In a realm where a deer's world and a wolf's world overlap in the same territory and neither sees what the other sees, the question has obvious urgency.

choices.text: Sit and listen

outcome.text: A practitioner meets your eyes in the reflection before turning around. They can teach Enchantment. The lake makes everything seem like a fair price.

choices.text: Walk away from the still water

outcome.text: You step back. The image on the water holds for a moment longer than it should, then dissolves.

animal_crossroads_stupa.title: Crossroads Stupa
animal_crossroads_stupa.text: Where the old game trails intersect, someone built a stupa centuries ago. The mortar between the stones includes offerings pressed in during construction — seeds, feathers, a cracked egg. Butter lamps burn at the base. The place smells of juniper smoke and something that has been burning for a very long time.

choices.text: Approach the stupa

outcome.text: A practitioner emerges from behind the stupa. Summoning magic — the crossroads is the right place for it. Gold is the price.

choices.text: Observe from a distance

outcome.text: You watch the butter lamps in the wind. Some things are better left undisturbed.

animal_eternal_fire.title: Temple of the Eternal Fire
animal_eternal_fire.text: The fire burns at the entrance to a cave, or near a volcanic vent, or at the base of an ancient tree struck by lightning and somehow still alive — wherever the ground produces heat that can be consecrated. The priests who tend it wear white and speak rarely. Creatures of many species come to pay respects. The fire does not discriminate.

choices.text: Approach the priests

outcome.text: A priest turns from the flame and regards you. He names the spells, and then the prices.

choices.text: Pay your respects and leave

outcome.text: You bow before the flame and step back. The fire reflected in your eyes for some time after.

animal_ocean_teahouse.title: Tide Shelter
animal_ocean_teahouse.text: A structure built into a sea cliff, half-submerged at high tide and bone-dry at low. A fire burns in a sealed alcove. Along the benches: naga, karka, and silhouettes you don't immediately place. The keeper is a broad and unhurried makara current who settled down forty years ago and has been pouring the same tea blend since. Nobody asks the recipe.

choices.text: Sit down

outcome.text: You take a seat. The current sets down a cup without asking.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You keep going. The smell of salt and smoke follows you out of the cliff.

animal_forest_teahouse.title: Forest Teahouse
animal_forest_teahouse.text: A platform structure high in the canopy, reachable by rope bridges from three directions. The vanara who run it have been doing so since before any of them can remember. The tea is brewed from forest herbs you don't recognize and tastes like rain, bark, and something that is not quite spice. It is very good.

choices.text: Sit down

outcome.text: You take a platform seat. A vanara sets down cups without ceremony.

choices.text: A teahouse a hundred feet up. Do this properly.

outcome.text:
You do the whole form on a swaying platform in the canopy, which is objectively ridiculous and which the proprietor watches with total seriousness.

At the end she brings out the other pot — the one that does not get offered — and does the form back at you.

choices.text: You are up before the canopy is light. So is she.

outcome.text:
The proprietor is doing the first firing of the day when you come up the rope ladder, and there is a particular understanding between people who are awake at that hour by choice.

You get the first pot. The first pot is not the same as the others and she does not explain why.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: The smell of forest tea follows you along the rope bridge.

animal_meadow_teahouse.title: Watering Hole Teahouse
animal_meadow_teahouse.text: A low structure at the edge of the great watering hole, where the land slopes gently down to the water. The truce of thirst holds here — every creature in the meadow observes it, because the keeper enforces it, and the keeper has been here longer than any of them. Inside: food, drink, and improbable peace.

choices.text: Sit down

outcome.text: You take a table. Nobody challenges you. This is the truce.

choices.text: Everything that lives here comes to this water eventually.

outcome.text:
Everything does, and everything talks, and a watering hole in the dry season is the single most informative place on the plain.

You leave knowing which route the migration will take, which is worth more than the tea cost.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You walk past the watering hole without stopping. The smell of water and cooking carries far on open ground.

animal_ocean_mercenary_guild.title: Mercenary Guild
animal_ocean_mercenary_guild.text: A fortified reef structure flying a plain banner — the same universal mercenary symbol, translated into something that can survive salt water. Inside, armed figures clean weapons or sleep. The work available in the ocean is different from the work available on land, and the going rate reflects the depth.

choices.text: Browse their services

outcome.text: The quartermaster produces a list. Rates, availability, terms.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You leave the mercenaries to their maintenance.

animal_forest_mercenary_guild.title: Mercenary Guild
animal_forest_mercenary_guild.text: A fortified outpost at the forest edge, flying a plain black banner between two old trees. The figures inside are armoured in hide and shell-plate — practical for the terrain. They look up when you enter with the universal expression of people who do this professionally.

choices.text: Browse their services

outcome.text: The quartermaster opens a case and waits.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You leave the mercenaries to their sharpening.

animal_meadow_mercenary_guild.title: Mercenary Guild
animal_meadow_mercenary_guild.text: A stockaded compound at a crossroads of migration routes, flying the universal mercenary banner on a pole tall enough to be seen from a distance. Inside, armoured figures play dice and argue rates. The work in the open meadow is the most visible and the most dangerous, and the prices reflect that.

choices.text: Browse their services

outcome.text: The quartermaster nods and produces a list. Standard rates. Meadow surcharge.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You skirt the compound and keep moving.

animal_ocean_training_camp.title: Naga Training Grounds
animal_ocean_training_camp.text: A reef plateau where naga warriors train daily — the drills are ancient and precise. They accept outsiders who show genuine commitment. The water here slows everything and makes every technique twice as demanding, which is the point.

choices.text: Ask about training

outcome.text: A senior naga warrior looks you over once. 'Two sessions. Choose carefully.'

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: The drills continue without you.

animal_forest_training_camp.title: Tracker's Training Ground
animal_forest_training_camp.text: A clearing used by those who hunt without being hunted — trackers, scouts, the nimble-fingered and the quick-footed. The vanara here share techniques that have been refined over many generations in this specific forest. Some of it translates; all of it is worth knowing.

choices.text: Ask about training

outcome.text: A vanara elder with patient eyes names two skills. 'Which two? Choose once.'

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You leave the clearing. The forest returns to its own lesson.

animal_meadow_training_camp.title: Open-Field Training Ground
animal_meadow_training_camp.text: A camp at the edge of the open plain where fighters train in the exposed, unforgiving style demanded by meadow combat — no cover, long sight lines, everything decided by strength and endurance. The yaksha veterans who run it have a simple philosophy: you learn to take a hit, and then you learn to give one back harder.

choices.text: Ask about training

outcome.text: 'We can teach two things. Once each. Make your choices.'

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: The veteran returns to drilling her students.

animal_ocean_town_weapons.title: Town
animal_ocean_town_weapons.text: A trading post built into a sea cliff and expanded outward on platform structures above the tideline. Karka shell-wrights and naga-forged spear merchants dominate the market. The clang of metalwork reaches out into open water. Most things for sale here were made to puncture something.

choices.text: Enter the market

outcome.text: You push through to the main stalls.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You skirt the settlement along the reef.

animal_ocean_town_magic.title: Town
animal_ocean_town_magic.text: A settlement built around a thermal vent, where the rising current brings strange minerals and stranger ideas. Water mages and naga sorcerers work from alcoves along the main tunnel. The air smells of sulfur and concentration. Someone is always arguing about the nature of current.

choices.text: Enter the settlement

outcome.text: You find the practitioners' quarter.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You leave the argument unresolved.

animal_ocean_town_supplies.title: Town
animal_ocean_town_supplies.text: A market platform on stilts above the tidal flat. Everything needed to survive the reef and deep water — preserved food, medicine, rope, breathing equipment. The sign reads: WHAT YOU NEED. NO QUESTIONS. The price is printed underneath, which saves time.

choices.text: Enter the market

outcome.text: The shopkeeper nods without looking up.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You keep going.

animal_forest_town_weapons.title: Town
animal_forest_town_weapons.text: A market at the forest's edge where different territories agree, briefly, to exchange. Dura shell-wright craftsmanship, vanara jugaad improvisation, shardula-claw handles on daggers sold by gana traders who got them somewhere no one is explaining. The weapons here are practical and tell stories.

choices.text: Enter the market

outcome.text: You push through the stalls.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You skirt the settlement and continue into the trees.

animal_forest_town_magic.title: Town
animal_forest_town_magic.text: A forest settlement where the mycelium network runs under every building and the practitioners who use it for communication have built a small trade in that adjacency. Alchemy, earth magic, summoning — the disciplines that grow from understanding what is underground. The shelves smell of soil and something fermented.

choices.text: Enter the settlement

outcome.text: You find the practitioners' stalls.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You leave the forest scholars to their arguments.

animal_forest_town_supplies.title: Town
animal_forest_town_supplies.text: A clearing settlement where four game trails meet. Sounder matrons and herb-walkers tend most of the stalls. Food preserved in bark and clay, medicines extracted from things most travelers walk past without recognizing, tools for the deep forest. It is honest trade in a place that doesn't demand credentials.

choices.text: Enter the market

outcome.text: The matron at the nearest stall sizes you up and names a fair price.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You keep walking. The smell of drying herbs follows you down the trail.

animal_meadow_town_weapons.title: Town
animal_meadow_town_weapons.text: An armorer's compound at a crossroads of migration routes, built low and solid to survive the open-ground seasons. Dura shell-wright work alongside yaksha-enchanted blades and khadga-horn handles. The merchants here have traveled to get here and priced accordingly. Everything for sale is worth carrying a long way.

choices.text: Enter the compound

outcome.text: You find the weapons hall.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You continue across the open ground.

animal_meadow_town_magic.title: Town
animal_meadow_town_magic.text: A settlement gathered around a yaksha standing stone, which functions as both landmark and practice anchor. Enchantment, earth magic, white healing — the disciplines that thrive in open country where the sky is visible and the earth is close. The practitioners here are travelers themselves, stopping as they always stop.

choices.text: Enter the settlement

outcome.text: You find the practitioners' quarter around the standing stone.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You leave the stone to its practitioners.

animal_meadow_town_supplies.title: Town
animal_meadow_town_supplies.text: A trading post at the great watering hole, where the migration routes converge and every creature passes through eventually. The merchants here have learned not to ask where anyone is going. Essential goods for the long traversal: food for crossing open ground, medicine for what open ground does to you, equipment for what you find at the end of it.

choices.text: Enter the market

outcome.text: The shopkeeper glances up briefly and goes back to counting stock.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: You keep moving. The watering hole glitters to your left.

events._comment_domain_guilds: === DOMAIN GUILDS — animal realm special locations ===

naga_palace.title: The Naga Palace
naga_palace.text: A coral arch rises from the reef, inscribed with naga glyphs marking territorial sovereignty. Two naga warriors flank the entrance but do not move to stop you. Beyond the arch, chambers of living coral lit by bioluminescent algae descend into the deep. Water magic and enchantment traditions have been practiced here without interruption since before the reef was reef.

choices.text: Ask to study here

outcome.text: A court official receives you with formal courtesy. They have everything the ocean's magic traditions offer. The price is calibrated to what you can pay, which means they already know.

choices.text: Observe the court protocol and withdraw respectfully

outcome.text:
You bow in the naga manner — low, without breaking eye contact — and withdraw. The court watches. A minor official nods very slightly.

You have not been insulted. In naga terms, this is an achievement.

choices.text: You have been ambushed by this before.

outcome.text:
The arch alone would have done it. You stand in front of it for some time with the specific helplessness of somebody who knows exactly what is happening to them and cannot speed it up.

The naga are used to this. One of them waits with you.

choices.text: Withdraw without seeking entry

outcome.text: You turn and leave the arch behind. The two warriors watch you go without expression.

ancient_banyan.title: The Ancient Banyan
ancient_banyan.text:
No one told you the tree existed, but you found it anyway. The banyan's aerial roots form a labyrinth; its canopy covers a quarter mile in every direction. The Vanara Elder sits in the first great fork, weaving something from spider silk and what you eventually realize is solidified starlight.

The tree has the attention of something older than itself. Earth magic and summoning traditions have always known about this place.

choices.text: Approach the Elder and ask to study

outcome.text: The Elder looks down from the fork with unhurried eyes. She names a price for her teaching. It is not small.

choices.text: Sit beneath the roots in silence

outcome.text: You sit with your back against a root as wide as a wall and close your eyes. The tree breathes. You breathe. After a time — you cannot say how long — something shifts: a sense of patience that is not your own, accumulated over centuries, seeping in through the bark.

choices.text: Walk away from the ancient tree

outcome.text: You leave the labyrinth of roots behind. The canopy covers you until you are out of the grove, and then the light returns all at once.

termite_cathedral.title: Termite Cathedral
termite_cathedral.text: The mound rises fifteen feet, engineered with an architect's precision for temperature and airflow. Carved archways mark the entrance in a script older than any living tradition. Inside, something hums at a frequency felt in the chest rather than heard by the ear. Yaksha practitioners and bhramara allies have used this place as a center of earth-consciousness work for as long as the mound has stood.

choices.text: Seek instruction

outcome.text: A yaksha practitioner emerges from the main chamber. Earth magic, summoning, and the basics of alchemy — the cathedral has all three. She names the prices plainly.

choices.text: Leave an offering at the base of the mound

outcome.text: You set your offering at the carved archway and stand back. The hum shifts frequency very slightly — just once. You take that as acknowledgement.

choices.text: Fifteen feet of engineering and nobody drew the plans.

outcome.text:
You spend the afternoon working out the ventilation, which is the part that should not be possible, and by evening you have it: the mound breathes on a temperature differential and the whole structure is a lung.

You will be thinking about this for weeks.

choices.text: Move on

outcome.text: The hum follows you for longer than the mound is visible.

birds_congress.title: Conference of the Birds
birds_congress.text:
The great assembly tree rises alone on a ridge where forest meets meadow — visible from both territories, which is why it was chosen. Every bird of the realm comes here when the season is right. Kapota and shyena roost three branches apart in a truce older than memory.

A kapota elder calls the session to order with a chant that names every species present. You recognize the structure: a congress, a parliament. They are looking for something. They are, in the old story, always looking for the Simurgh. And, in the old story, they are the Simurgh — but they haven't arrived at that part yet.

choices.text: Attend the congress and learn from the teachings

outcome.text: A kapota messenger escorts you to an observer's perch. Air magic, space magic, and the white traditions of the sky practitioners — all available. The price is a story you haven't told anyone else.

choices.text: Listen to the full session without speaking

outcome.text:
You sit at the base of the tree for the full congress — hours, perhaps longer. The birds speak in twenty overlapping languages and you understand almost none of it.

But near the end, when the elder names the purpose of the journey, you understand that part. Not the words — the shape of it. The search that finds itself.

choices.text: You can name most of the delegations from here.

outcome.text:
You can, and you do, quietly, and the naming turns out to be the credential — the congress has been addressed by a great many people who did not know a shyena from a garuda.

You are given a place at the lower branches, which is further in than visitors go.

choices.text: Leave the birds to their congress

outcome.text: You descend from the ridge. The chant continues behind you, diminishing into the wind.

bone_forest.title: The Bone Forest
bone_forest.text:
The bones are organized, not scattered. Skulls face east, spines curve north, limb bones arranged radially from the center as though following a diagram. Something has been doing this for a very long time. In the center of the clearing, a practitioner in dark robes performs a slow ritual over a fresh death — a khadga, enormous, at peace.

They don't look up when you approach.

'Looking for death lessons,' they say. 'Or life ones. They're the same here.'

choices.text: Ask to learn

outcome.text: The practitioner rises, unhurried. Black magic and summoning — the traditions that work with what remains. They name the spells and the prices without ceremony.

choices.text: Help with the ritual

outcome.text:
You take your position across the body from the practitioner and mirror their movements as best you can. The ritual has its own grammar; you improvise where you don't know the words.

The khadga's presence, enormous even in death, seems to hold still for a moment. Then it passes, as presences do.

choices.text: The skulls face east. Somebody decided that.

outcome.text:
Somebody decided it, and kept deciding it, for what must be generations — the arrangement is maintained, not merely made.

You find the current keeper by looking for who has been walking here recently, and they are glad to be found.

choices.text: Leave respectfully

outcome.text: You bow toward the center of the bone arrangement and leave without disturbing anything. The practitioner has already returned to their work.

animal_sigh_of_relief.title: The Great Stag
animal_sigh_of_relief.text:
In a forest clearing — or on an open hillside, or at the edge of the reef where the light reaches — you find a great stag standing alone. His rack is hung with orchids. Around him, smaller creatures have gathered: a rabbit, two kapota pigeons, a young vanara sitting cross-legged. The stag is lowering his head, letting them feed from the flowers and mosses growing between his antlers.

No one has asked him to do this. He simply knows it is time.

choices.text: Meditate in the presence of this

outcome.text:
You settle into stillness. The stag's attention moves over you once, and then returns to the gathered creatures. That moment of attention is enough — something clear passes through you and keeps going.

You remember that generosity is not sacrifice. It is just knowing it is time.

choices.text: Leave some of your food for those gathered

outcome.text:
You set down what you can spare and step back. The vanara reaches it first, then shares without being asked.

The stag watches. He has seen this before — the chain of giving. It always surprises him a little.

choices.text: Watch from the treeline

outcome.text:
You stay at the edge of the clearing and watch until the stag lifts his head and the gathered creatures drift away. Then the clearing is just a clearing again.

You carry the image of it for a long time.

choices.text: Approach and take from what is being offered

outcome.text:
You walk into the clearing. The gathered creatures scatter. The stag raises his head and looks at you with amber eyes.

He does not move. He does not attack. He simply regards you until you leave.

You feel, for a long time afterward, that you have been recognized.

animal_crossroads_shrine.title: Crossroads Shrine
animal_crossroads_shrine.text: Where three animal trails cross, someone built a cairn of stones. Prayer flags, thread, feathers pressed flat between layers of bark, bones arranged with obvious care — offerings that don't specify any particular tradition but cover their bases. A single butter lamp burns in a notch in the topmost stone.

choices.text: Leave an offering

outcome.text: You add something of yours to the cairn. The butter lamp flickers once in still air.

choices.text: Sit for a moment and breathe

outcome.text: You sit at the base of the cairn. At a crossroads, all directions are valid — this is what makes them sacred. For a moment you remember all of them.

choices.text: Somebody built this where the animals cross, not where people do.

outcome.text:
That is the whole point of it and almost nobody notices. The cairn faces the trails, the offerings are the kind an animal would take, and the person who built it was making an argument.

You add to it in the same spirit.

choices.text: Pass without disturbing anything

outcome.text: You leave the lamp to its burning.

animal_ocean_naga_greeting.title: The Naga's Greeting
animal_ocean_naga_greeting.text:
A naga rises from the reef ahead — long, scaled, regarding you with amber eyes that haven't blinked. She circles once, slowly, then stops with her coils wound loosely around a pillar of coral.

'You are not of this water,' she says. It is not quite a question.

She is assessing you. This happens every time something new arrives in the ocean realm. She does not find it alarming — only relevant.

choices.text: Introduce yourself and explain your purpose

outcome.text:
You speak plainly. She listens without interrupting, which is the naga equivalent of a warm welcome.

When you finish, she unwinds from the coral pillar and gestures toward the open water. 'The western currents carry the faster trade. The eastern ones are watched.' She does not explain by whom.

You have been received.

choices.text: Stand your ground without speaking

outcome_success.text:
You hold her gaze without flinching. She is silent for a long moment.

'Ah,' she says finally, and uncoils. She seems, somehow, pleased. 'The quiet ones always know where they're going.'

outcome_failure.text:
You hold it as long as you can, which is not as long as you thought.

The eyes are wrong in a way that takes a moment to locate — there is no lid, and no blink, and nothing behind them that recognises the courtesy you are attempting. When you look away she does not comment on it, which is worse.

'Mm,' she says, and coils back. The audience is over, and you have been placed somewhere in her ordering of things.

choices.text: Offer a gift

outcome.text:
She examines the gift with the patience of someone for whom time is elastic. Then she accepts it.

In return, she describes three things: where the food is, where the danger is, and where the old temple lies. You did not ask about the temple. She offers it anyway, as though it were simply the correct exchange.

animal_karka_reef_warden.title: Reef Warden
animal_karka_reef_warden.text:
The pass through the coral barrier is narrow and long. Halfway through, a karka fills it completely — shell the width of the passage, claws braced against the coral walls, eyes fixed on you.

She is not sleeping. She has been watching since you entered the corridor.

The thermal vent behind her produces a faint heat that rises through the passage. This is her vent. This is her pass. These things are not in question.

choices.text: Attempt to negotiate passage

outcome_success.text:
You speak to her in terms she respects — this is her territory, you acknowledge it; you need to pass, you explain why; you will not return unless invited.

Her eyes do not change. But after a long pause, she steps aside — just enough. The passage is tight. She watches every inch of it.

outcome_failure.text:
You make the argument. It is a decent argument, and she listens to all of it with her claws folded.

'No,' she says, when you have finished. She does not explain, and it becomes clear she does not consider an explanation to be part of the transaction. The reef is hers. You are not from the reef.

You go the long way, and it costs you most of a day.

choices.text: Offer gold as a crossing toll

outcome.text:
She looks at the gold. She looks at you. She reaches out one claw and takes it with surprising delicacy.

Then she moves aside. The passage is yours. She adds the gold to a pile you hadn't noticed — there is a system here, practiced over years. You are not the first to find this more efficient than the alternative.

choices.text: Fight your way through

outcome.text: She braces. Her claws score the coral walls. Whatever comes next, she will not move from this vent.

choices.text: Retreat and find another route

outcome.text:
You back out of the passage the way you came. There are other passes — you will find them.

Behind you, the karka returns to her vigil without comment. This happens, too.

animal_ridge_predator.title: Ridge Predator
animal_ridge_predator.text:
The pass through the thorn ridge narrows to a ledge barely wide enough to walk single file. At its midpoint, something large sits very still.

A shardula — a leopard of immense size, pale as the rock, watching you from exactly the spot the path must cross. His tail moves once, slowly. He does not rise.

He is neither blocking nor permitting. He is simply here, as he has been here many times before, watching what comes through.

choices.text: Make the formal greeting between predator-kin

outcome.text:
You lower your gaze, expose your throat briefly, and then meet his eyes again without aggression — the grammar of predator recognition. It takes composure you didn't know you had.

He considers this for a long moment. Then he stands, turns, and walks to the edge of the ledge, leaving the path clear. He watches you cross without looking away.

choices.text: Proceed slowly, making no threatening gesture

outcome_success.text:
You walk forward with the deliberate calm of something that does not consider itself prey. Each step measured. Gaze steady.

He watches the whole crossing. When you reach the other side, he blinks once — slowly — and looks away. You have been assessed and found unremarkable. In predator terms, this is the best outcome.

outcome_failure.text:
Halfway across, someone's foot finds the one loose stone on the ridge.

It is a small sound. It is enough. He is up and moving before the stone has finished falling, and the crossing becomes a run, and the run becomes a scramble down the scree on the far side with a good deal less dignity than anyone intended.

He does not follow past the ridgeline. He does not need to — he has made his point, and you are bleeding from the places the scree found.

choices.text: Set down some food and step back

outcome.text:
You set a portion of food on the rock and retreat two steps. He looks at the offering, looks at you, and then — with the total lack of embarrassment of something that does not require gratitude — takes it.

The path is yours.

choices.text: He is enormous and beautiful and you want to say hello.

outcome.text:
You want to. Everything in you wants to, and the part of you that knows better is losing the argument until somebody takes your elbow.

You cross without incident and spend the rest of the day defending the impulse, badly.

choices.text: Challenge him

outcome.text: He rises from the rock in one fluid motion. His ears flatten. He has done this before.

animal_boss_simha_king.title: The King of Beasts
animal_boss_simha_king.text:
The oldest part of the forest is where he sits — where the trees are so wide you could sleep in their roots and the canopy blocks all direct sun. The simha king does not rise when you approach.

He is the largest lion you have ever imagined possible. His mane is the color of old wood. He is already ancient in legends that are themselves old. The portal to the Human Realm shimmers behind him in the roots of the oldest tree.

He is not blocking it, exactly. He is simply here, as he has always been here — at the threshold, at the end of the animal realm, where the path changes.

His gaze crosses your party without hurry, taking careful measure.

choices.text: Approach peacefully and bow

outcome.text:
You approach slowly and bow — low and long. When you rise, he has not moved, but something in his posture has changed: the calculation has left it.

'You have learned something here,' he says, in a voice like the ground settling. 'Go forward. Don't waste it.'

He stands and walks aside. The portal is clear.

choices.text: Offer tribute worthy of a king

outcome_success.text:
You present what you have with the ceremony the moment deserves. He examines it without touching it — not the goods, but the gesture.

'Adequate,' he says. He steps aside without further ceremony. 'The realm of humans is expecting something. Try not to disappoint it.'

outcome_failure.text:
He looks at what you have brought for a long, unhurried moment.

'You have given me,' he says, 'what you could spare.' There is no anger in it. That is the difficulty — there is nothing in it at all. 'Tribute is what you cannot spare. Otherwise it is only tidying.'

He returns it. The goods are yours again and worth rather less than they were.

choices.text: Prove your worth in combat

outcome.text:
He rises slowly — no urgency, no anger. He has simply agreed to your terms. His voice carries one last note before the charge:

'Good. I wanted to see if you could.'

choices.text: Attempt to find another way through

outcome_success.text:
You study the roots, the shadows, the angles. There is a gap — not much of one, but enough.

As you slip through, his voice reaches you from the center of the clearing: 'Clever. But you'll find cleverness has limits, further on.'

He does not pursue.

outcome_failure.text:
The gap is there. It is exactly where you judged it to be, and it closes while you are still committed to it.

He has not moved quickly. He has simply been in the place you were going to be, for some time, waiting to see whether you had understood the ground as well as you believed.

'No,' he says, almost kindly. 'Again, or not at all.'

animal_ocean_naga_patrol.title: Naga Patrol
animal_ocean_naga_patrol.text:
Four naga rise out of the channel in formation, coils turning slow circles to hold position against the current. The lead wears a collar of hammered silver and carries no weapon — she does not appear to think she needs one.

"You are walking on the roof of someone's house," she says. "State whose permission you carry."

choices.text: Answer with steel
Say you carry no one's permission and ask for hers

outcome.text: The honesty surprises her into stillness. "No one says that." She considers you for a long moment, then flicks her tail and the formation opens. "Walk quickly. Someone less patient holds the next channel."

choices.text: Greet her in the old water-tongue

outcome.text: You shape the greeting the way the current shapes stone — slowly, with the vowels drowned. Her whole posture changes. "You were taught properly. By whom?" You do not answer, and she decides not to press. She gives you the safe line through the reef and the name of a tidal pool worth visiting.

choices.text: Wait for the current to turn and slip through behind them

outcome_success.text: The tide changes and their formation drifts three lengths downstream to compensate. You are across the open water before it closes.

outcome_failure.text: The lead's head turns before you have taken four steps. "They always try the tide," she says, almost bored.

animal_ocean_karka_standoff.title: Reef Guardian
animal_ocean_karka_standoff.text:
A karka the size of a fishing boat has wedged itself into the only gap in the reef wall. Its shell is crusted with a century of coral growth — it has been here long enough to become part of the reef.

One claw opens. Closes. It has not decided about you yet.

choices.text: Force the gap
Set food on the rock and step back

outcome.text: The claw takes the offering with a delicacy that seems impossible for something that size. It shifts perhaps a hand's width — enough, if you go sideways and do not touch the shell.

choices.text: Read the growth on its shell and speak to its age

outcome.text: You count the coral bands aloud — the lean years, the warm years, the year something tore a notch from its left claw. By the time you finish it has lowered itself flat to the rock, which you understand is not submission but welcome. Behind it, in a hollow it has clearly been guarding, are things the sea brought and it never ate.

choices.text: Climb the reef wall over the top of it

outcome_success.text: Coral opens your palms in a dozen places but the karka never looks up. You come down on the far side bleeding and past it.

outcome_failure.text: A handhold gives. You land badly, directly in front of it, and the claw is already opening.

animal_ocean_matsya_ambush.title: Matsya Hunters
animal_ocean_matsya_ambush.text:
The water on both sides of the sandbar goes suddenly, completely still — the stillness of a great many things deciding to stop moving at once.

Then the matsya break surface in a ring around you, spears already levelled. They have done this before. They are not in a hurry.

choices.text: Fight your way off the sandbar
Put down your packs and let them take what they want

outcome.text: They take methodically, without malice, leaving you your water and one blade between you. As they sink away the nearest one taps her spear twice on the sand — which you will later learn is how the matsya say 'nothing personal'.

choices.text: Compliment the ambush — the placement, the patience, the silence

outcome.text: You describe their own trap back to them: the two swimmers who went wide an hour ago, the deliberate noise upstream, the way they let you commit to the bar before closing. The ring loosens. Professionals recognising a professional. They let you go and, unprompted, tell you where the next three ambushes are set.

choices.text: Pick the weakest point in the ring and charge it

outcome_success.text: You go through the youngest of them shoulder-first and are in deep water before the ring can turn. They do not follow past the drop-off.

outcome_failure.text: The young one you chose is not the weak point. He was bait.

animal_ocean_makara_feeding.title: Makara Feeding
animal_ocean_makara_feeding.text:
Something enormous is feeding in the shallows ahead. The makara's back breaks the surface in a long slow arc, over and over, as it works through a shoal that has nowhere left to go. The water is pink for fifty paces.

It has not noticed you. It is, for the moment, extremely busy.

choices.text: Attack while it is distracted
Lie flat and wait for it to finish

outcome.text: It takes most of an hour. You spend it face-down on hot rock listening to a thing the size of a barge eat. When the water finally stills, you find the shoal's survivors stranded in the pools — more fish than your party can carry.

choices.text: Read the water and time your crossing between its passes

outcome.text: The makara's rhythm is written in the current as clearly as a heartbeat. You cross in the trough of each pass, four paces at a time, and are on the far shore before it lifts its head. It never knew you were there — which, you reflect, is the only victory available here.

choices.text: Dart in and take what it has driven ashore

outcome_success.text: You work the tideline while it works the deep, and you are gone with an armload before the arc of its back turns your way.

outcome_failure.text: The arc of its back does turn your way. It has been aware of you for some time and simply had not finished eating.

animal_ocean_makara_tribute.title: Makara's Toll
animal_ocean_makara_tribute.text: A line of poles has been driven into the seabed across the whole width of the channel, and from each hangs an offering — fish, coins, a bronze bell, a child's carved boat. At the centre, coiled in water too deep to see the bottom of, something very large is waiting to see what you add to the line.

choices.text: Hang gold on the empty pole

outcome.text: The coil beneath shifts once, settling, and the channel is simply open. Whatever governs this arrangement, it is scrupulous about its side of it.

choices.text: Walk the line without adding anything

outcome.text: You are two poles along when the water beneath you stops being water and starts being throat.

choices.text: Make the offering properly — with the words, not just the goods

outcome.text: You hang the offering and then speak over it, naming the water, the channel, and the thing beneath by the titles owed to something that has held one place since before the reef existed. The response is not sound. It is the entire channel going warm, all at once, like a held breath released. On the far bank you find a second offering waiting: yours, returned, with something added.

choices.text: Somebody set this toll. Tolls have terms.

outcome.text:
They do, and the poles record them — the makara's terms are carved on the landward side of the third post, which nobody reads because nobody thinks of a makara as an institution.

It turns out you have already overpaid by walking this far, and you say so.

choices.text: Take from the poles instead of adding to them

outcome_success.text: You lift the bronze bell and three purses without disturbing the line, and are across and gone. Somewhere behind you the coil sleeps on. You have gotten away with it. That is not the same as it not counting.

outcome_failure.text: The bell rings. Of course the bell rings. That is what the bell is for.

animal_ocean_naga_court.title: Naga Court
animal_ocean_naga_court.text:
The court convenes in a natural amphitheatre of coral, the assembled naga arranged by age with the oldest lowest and deepest. They are hearing a grievance: two families, one oyster bed, four generations of argument.

The proceedings pause. Every head turns. A visitor is, apparently, more interesting than the oyster bed.

choices.text: Bow and watch the proceedings in silence

outcome.text: You sit through four hours of argument conducted entirely in a register of extreme courtesy, and understand perhaps a third of it. At the end nobody has won and everybody seems satisfied. The naga consider this an excellent outcome and are pleased you stayed.

choices.text: Ask leave to trade with the court

outcome.text: An attendant is detached from the proceedings to deal with you — politely, and with the air of someone glad of the excuse.

choices.text: Offer an outsider's judgment on the oyster bed

outcome.text: You propose that the bed be worked by both families and the harvest split by the tide that brought it — an arrangement neither could have offered without losing face, but which a stranger can suggest freely. There is a very long silence. Then the eldest laughs, a sound like a cave flooding, and the court adopts it on the spot. Four generations, settled by someone who will be gone by evening.

choices.text: The court is deciding where to put you.

outcome.text:
It decides quickly and it decides well, and the seat you are given has a view of the proceedings that a trade delegation would have argued for.

You are aware this has nothing to do with anything you have done. It is still the better seat.

choices.text: A court is only people, and people are your subject.

outcome.text:
Within an hour you are on genuinely warm terms with two junior members of a delegation and one archivist, and the archivist is the one who matters.

What you learn from her is not on the agenda and would not have been raised at it.

choices.text: Ask the eldest what the naga remember of the realms above

outcome.text: "We remember all of it," she says. "That is the affliction. Your kind forgets and calls it healing." She tells you three things about the world above the water. Two of them you already knew. The third rearranges something.

animal_ocean_pearl_merchant.title: Pearl Merchant
animal_ocean_pearl_merchant.text:
She has set out her stock on a square of blue cloth weighted at the corners with stones: pearls, mostly, but also polished shell, sea-glass, and a few things that are clearly older than her trade and probably not hers to sell.

"Everything here came out of something living," she says cheerfully. "Prices reflect that."

choices.text: Look over the stock

outcome.text: She names prices without haggling and watches your hands the entire time.

choices.text: Nothing you need today

outcome.text: "Come back when the tide's out," she says. "Better stock, worse prices."

choices.text: Point out that one of her 'pearls' is a carved bone bead

outcome.text: She goes very still, then picks up the bead and turns it over twice. "Sold to me as a deep-water pearl. Three years ago." She is not angry with you. She is calculating something. Then she hands you a genuine one — small, flawed, real. "For the education. I have an appointment to keep with a man in the shallows."

choices.text: Pearls have a price and it is not the one on the cloth.

outcome.text:
You go through the stock stone by stone, noting the flaws out loud in a tone of mild regret.

By the end she has halved two prices to stop you doing it to the rest, which is exactly the mechanism you were relying on.

choices.text: Ask which bed the good ones come from, and go get your own

outcome_success.text: She tells you, laughing, certain the depth will beat you. It nearly does. You come up grey-lipped and shaking with three good ones in your fist, and she buys two on the spot at a price that suggests she has revised her opinion.

outcome_failure.text: The pressure turns you back twice, and the third time something large moves past you in the dark and you surface with nothing but a great deal of respect for her profession.

animal_ocean_karka_merchant.title: Shell-Wright's Stall
animal_ocean_karka_merchant.text:
The karka has built his workshop out of his own moults — a spiral of discarded shells, each larger than the last, the oldest ones worn smooth as furniture. Inside, he is fitting plate to a customer's cracked carapace with the total absorption of a craftsman who has forgotten there is a world.

He raises one claw: *wait*. Then, a moment later: *now*.

choices.text: See what the shell-wright has made

outcome.text: He lays out work in shell, chitin and salvaged metal, and names prices in a clicking dialect that somehow leaves no ambiguity.

choices.text: Leave him to his work

outcome.text: He has already forgotten you. The claw moves; the plate settles a hair truer.

choices.text: Offer a smith's technique in trade for a shell-wright's

outcome.text: You show him how a lap joint is scarfed in metal; he shows you how a moult is scored so it splits along a chosen line instead of the line it wants. Neither of you can fully use the other's craft. Both of you leave better. He presses salvage on you and will not discuss payment.

choices.text: Commission a repair on your own gear

outcome.text: He works on your armour for two hours without once looking at you, and hands it back better than it was when it was new. There is a small spiral scored inside the collar. His mark, presumably. Or a joke.

animal_ocean_sunken_ship.title: Sunken Ship
animal_ocean_sunken_ship.text:
A trading vessel lies on her side in four fathoms, close enough to shore that her upper rail breaks the surface at low tide. She has been down long enough to grow a garden and not long enough for the cargo to have rotted.

Something has been at the hull. The tear in her side is not from rock.

choices.text: Leave the dead their ship

outcome.text: You walk the shoreline past her. At the low point of the tide the rail shows for a moment, like something surfacing to look.

choices.text: Work the accessible upper decks

outcome.text: The upper cabins are stripped — someone has been here — but the deck fittings are bronze and nobody bothered with them.

choices.text: Dive the flooded hold

outcome_success.text: Three trips down, lungs burning each time. The hold's manifest was accurate: bolts of oiled cloth still dry inside their wrapping, a strongbox, and a case of somebody's carefully packed instruments.

outcome_failure.text: A hatch swings shut above you in the dark and it takes a very bad half-minute to find the other way out. You surface with nothing, and stay sat on the rocks for a while.

choices.text: There is a hold. Everything good is in the hold.

outcome.text:
There is, and it is, and the water in it is black and the angle is wrong and you go down anyway.

You come up with more than the upper decks would have given and rather less breath than you went down with.

choices.text: Speak the rites for the crew before touching anything

outcome.text: You say the words over the water. Nothing visible happens, which is how it usually goes. But the hold, when you enter it afterwards, is simply a room full of goods rather than the other thing it had been — and the tear in the hull, you notice, is on the inside. Something got out. Whatever it was, it is long gone.

animal_ocean_naga_temple.title: Sunken Temple
animal_ocean_naga_temple.text:
The temple was built on dry land. That was a long time ago. Now the sea comes in through the doorway at every tide and goes out again, and the carvings on the inner walls have been polished featureless from the waist down and remain razor-sharp above.

The upper registers show naga teaching. The lower, worn away, presumably showed who they were teaching.

choices.text: This is not yours to enter

outcome.text: You leave it to the tide, which has been more patient with it than any worshipper.

choices.text: Explore the dry upper chambers

outcome.text: Salt, silence, and a stone box someone left behind in a hurry a very long time ago.

choices.text: Read what remains of the teaching registers

outcome.text: The sequence is a commentary on desire, carved by people who lived where the water always took things back. The final panel is worn to nothing, but the panel before it shows the teacher's hands open and empty, and you find you do not need the last one.

choices.text: It is a temple. The water is a detail.

outcome.text:
You go down and do the circuit, which underwater takes longer and hurts more and is in every other respect identical.

The naga who find you doing it are so thoroughly disarmed that the conversation afterwards starts from a position no negotiation would have reached.

choices.text: Sit through a full tide in the flooded nave

outcome.text: The water comes to your chest and goes away again and comes back. Somewhere in the fourth hour the distinction between the tide's patience and your own stops being useful. You get up when it is over without any clear sense of having decided to.

animal_ocean_thermal_vents.title: Thermal Vents
animal_ocean_thermal_vents.text:
Where the seabed cracks, the water boils. A forest of pale chimneys vents black smoke into cold water, and around each one lives a whole crowded world that has never seen the sun and would die within sight of it.

The karka farm these. There are tool-marks on the nearest chimney.

choices.text: Give the vents a wide berth

outcome.text: The water shimmers behind you for a long way.

choices.text: Harvest what grows on the cooler chimneys

outcome.text: The growth comes away in sheets, strange and rubbery and — according to every alchemist you have ever met — extremely valuable.

choices.text: Work the hot vents properly, with a chemist's care

outcome.text: You take from the seam where the boiling water meets the cold, which is where the interesting compounds precipitate and where a careless hand gets scalded to the bone. It takes hours. What you bring up is worth the hours.

choices.text: Dive between the chimneys to reach the deep seam

outcome_success.text: You read the plumes — which vent is steady, which is about to surge — and thread between them to the seam floor, where the good material has been collecting since before anyone was counting.

outcome_failure.text: A vent you had judged steady surges as you pass. The water is instantly, unsurvivably hot for about a second and a half, and you are only at the edge of it.

animal_ocean_current_crossing.title: Strong Current
animal_ocean_current_crossing.text: The channel here runs fast and cold between two rock shelves. It is not deep. It is simply moving faster than a person can stand up in, and it goes somewhere you cannot see.

choices.text: Take the long way around

outcome.text: Half a day of walking and no drama whatsoever. There is something to be said for it.

choices.text: Rope together and wade it

outcome_success.text: Four in a line, each holding the next, moving on the count. Halfway across the current takes the smallest of you off their feet and the rope does exactly what rope is for.

outcome_failure.text: The rope holds. The packs do not. You reach the far shelf intact and noticeably lighter.

choices.text: Cross on the surface

outcome.text: You walk over water that is trying very hard to be somewhere else, and it does not get a vote. The others follow in your footprints, which hold just long enough.

choices.text: Somebody has to be the anchor and it is obviously you.

outcome.text:
You take the upstream end and plant yourself, and the cold gets into your legs and stays there while five people cross a rope you are personally holding in place.

You go last. You are shaking by then and it does not matter.

choices.text: Roped or not, the bottom here is round stones.

outcome.text:
Round stones and a fast current and a foot that has never once been reliable on either.

You go down mid-channel and the rope saves you, which is what the rope is for, and the pack you were carrying is not saved by anything.

choices.text: Find the slack line the fish are using

outcome.text: There is a seam of nearly-still water behind a submerged boulder, and a queue of patient fish holding station in it. You use their road. It is knee-deep and calm the whole way.

animal_ocean_drowned_caravan.title: Drowned Caravan
animal_ocean_drowned_caravan.text:
The tide has gone out over a mudflat and left a caravan standing in it — carts, packs, a cooking pot still upright on its stones. Everything is exactly where it was set down. Nothing is broken.

There are no bodies, and no tracks leading away.

choices.text: Take what you can carry and move on quickly

outcome.text: You load up fast and do not look at the cooking pot, which has three bowls set beside it.

choices.text: Set the packs upright, say something, and leave it be

outcome.text: You do not know their names or their rites. You say the words you do know, badly, and go. The tide comes back in behind you and takes the cooking pot.

choices.text: Read the mud — find out what happened here

outcome.text: No struggle, no scatter, no drag-marks. Everyone set down what they were holding and walked into the water together, in step, and the last set of prints is the smallest. You take nothing from the caravan after that. Further up the flat you find a cache they had buried before it happened — the only thing here that was hidden rather than surrendered.

choices.text: Feel for what is still standing here

outcome.text: They have not gone. They are standing exactly where they stood, in the same arrangement, facing the water, and they have been standing there through every tide since. One of them notices you noticing. She raises a hand — not a warning. A greeting, from someone with nothing left to warn anyone about. You leave the goods and go.

animal_forest_rakshasa_ambush.title: Rakshasa Ambush
animal_forest_rakshasa_ambush.text:
The birds stopped a hundred paces back. You noticed, and kept walking, because there was nowhere else to walk.

He drops out of the canopy directly into your path — a rakshasa, orange-eyed and unhurried, blocking the trail with the relaxed posture of something that has already counted you and likes the number.

choices.text: Meet him
Back down the trail without turning around

outcome.text: You retreat facing him, slowly, for two hundred paces. He follows for one hundred and fifty of them and then simply stops, having established whatever he needed to establish. You go the long way.

choices.text: Make yourself expensive — show him the arithmetic

outcome.text: You do not threaten him. You simply plant, shift your grip, and let him read what taking you would cost. Rakshasa are predators, not gamblers. He tilts his head, makes a sound that might be a laugh, and steps off the trail to let you pass — then follows at fifty paces for an hour, just to be sure you leave.

choices.text: The birds stopped a hundred paces back. You stopped too.

outcome.text:
You stopped with them, which is why the party is already off the trail and in cover when the rakshasa commits to a charge at where you were going to be.

It is very fast. It is not faster than being somewhere else.

choices.text: He is too relaxed — look for the other one

outcome_success.text: There. Above and behind, flattened along a branch, the actual ambush. You point at her without looking away from him, and the whole shape of the encounter collapses. Caught out, they withdraw with what dignity they can — and leave the kill they had been guarding.

outcome_failure.text: You are still looking for the second one when she lands behind you.

animal_forest_shardula_territory.title: Marked Territory
animal_forest_shardula_territory.text:
Claw-marks at head height on every fourth trunk, running as far as you can see in both directions. The marks are fresh, deliberate, and evenly spaced — this is not an animal scratching. It is a boundary, maintained.

The forest beyond the line is very quiet.

choices.text: Cross the line

outcome.text: You are forty paces past the marks when the pale shape detaches from a trunk that it had, until that moment, appeared to be part of.

choices.text: Follow the boundary until it ends

outcome.text: It takes most of a day. The line ends at a river, and something pale watches you from the far bank the whole time you are fording — but the marks stop at the water, and so does she.

choices.text: Add your own mark beside hers and wait

outcome.text: You cut your mark at the same height, the same depth, and sit down with your back to it. She comes within the hour. For a long time she just looks at the two marks side by side. Then she cuts a third — above both — and withdraws. You have been given passage and put in your place simultaneously, which is, you gather, the shardula way of being generous.

choices.text: Cross without leaving a trace

outcome.text: Downwind, on stone and root, never breaking a stem. You are through her range and out the other side and she never knows — which is worth more than her permission would have been, and cost more to earn.

animal_forest_gana_pack.title: Gana Pack
animal_forest_gana_pack.text:
They do not surround you so much as *arrive around* you — six gana, drifting out of the undergrowth at intervals, each one taking a position that closes an option you had not yet realised you were relying on.

The last to appear is the smallest, and she is the one the others keep glancing at.

choices.text: Fight the pack
Put meat on the ground and keep walking

outcome.text: They let the food sit until you are forty paces on. Behind you there is a brief, businesslike scuffle over shares, and then nothing. You are not followed.

choices.text: Speak to the small one — the others already are

outcome.text: You ignore the big males entirely and address the small female directly, which is both correct and clearly unexpected. She holds your eye for an uncomfortably long time. Then she yawns — enormous, deliberate, a gesture of dismissal that is also a gesture of safe-conduct — and the whole pack loses interest at once. One of them walks you to the ridge, for reasons of its own.

choices.text: This is not an ambush. This is a working formation.

outcome.text:
It is the shape you would use yourself, if you had six people and needed them to arrive around something at once.

You say so, out loud, with the technical terms. The gana stop what they are doing and reconsider you from the beginning.

choices.text: Stand absolutely still and let them lose interest

outcome_success.text: Twenty minutes. Nobody moves; nobody blinks first, exactly, but the pack's attention frays the way attention does, and one by one they are simply elsewhere.

outcome_failure.text: Someone's nerve goes. A foot shifts. That is all it takes.

animal_forest_varaha_charge.title: Varaha Charge
animal_forest_varaha_charge.text:
You have walked into the middle of a sounder and the middle of a sounder is where the young are.

The boar between you and the trail is not large. The one coming through the undergrowth behind her at considerable speed is.

choices.text: Brace and meet the charge
Get everyone up a tree, immediately

outcome.text: Undignified, effective. The sounder mills below for half an hour, working itself down from fury to irritation to boredom, and moves off. Someone's pack does not survive the experience.

choices.text: Read the charge line and move the party off it

outcome.text: A varaha charge is a commitment, not a decision — she is going to arrive exactly where she is pointed. You get everyone four paces left and she goes past close enough to feel, and does not turn, because turning is not part of it. The sounder follows her through and the trail is clear.

choices.text: Do not climb. Stand.

outcome.text:
Standing still in front of a charging sounder is a terrible idea that happens to be the correct one, and you are the only person present capable of doing it.

The matron breaks off four feet short. She was never going to commit; she needed to see whether you would.

choices.text: Greet the matron the way a varaha would

outcome.text: You go down on one knee, put your eyes below hers, and make the low sound the old ones make when the sounder is settling for the night. The charge does not stop so much as forget itself. She stands over you breathing hard, and then, with enormous dignity, pretends none of it happened and shepherds her young past you into the trees.

animal_forest_vanara_toll.title: Vanara Toll
animal_forest_vanara_toll.text:
A rope bridge crosses the gorge, and it is in excellent repair, which in this forest means somebody maintains it, which means somebody charges for it.

Four vanara are sitting on the far anchor. One of them is holding your water-skin. You are still wearing your pack.

choices.text: Take the bridge by force
Pay the toll

outcome.text: The coins vanish. The water-skin comes back. So, unexpectedly, does a knife you had not noticed was missing, and a small carved bird that was never yours. "Overpayment," says the one holding it, with the air of someone who considers this a serious matter.

choices.text: Take something of theirs first

outcome.text: By the time you reach the far anchor you are holding the toll-keeper's belt, her tally-string, and the pin from the bridge's tensioner — which you hand back immediately, because you are not insane. The vanara are delighted. This is the funniest thing that has happened to them this season. You cross free and they wave you off like family.

choices.text: Tell them what you did at the last bridge.

outcome.text:
None of it happened. The vanara are, however, professionals of the form, and they can tell a good account from a true one and prefer the former.

You cross for a story instead of a coin. They will be telling your version by winter, improved.

choices.text: Make them laugh

outcome.text: It is not a good joke. It is a joke about a monkey, told to four monkeys, by someone standing over a very deep gorge — and the sheer nerve of it lands where wit would not have. They let you cross on the strength of it and demand you tell it again to the elder.

animal_forest_mycelium_tender.title: Mycelium Tender
animal_forest_mycelium_tender.text:
The varaha is on her knees in the leaf-litter with her snout an inch from the ground, doing something that is unmistakably horticulture. Around her, over perhaps an acre, the forest floor has been coaxed into patterns — fruiting bodies in arcs and spirals, each species where it does best.

"Don't step there," she says without looking up. "That one took nine years."

choices.text: Step carefully back the way you came

outcome.text: "Good," she says, still not looking up. It is the warmest thing anyone has said to you all week.

choices.text: Ask whether any of it is for trade

outcome.text: "Some." She sells you the ones that fruit fast and refuses to discuss the others. The transaction takes ten minutes and eight words.

choices.text: Offer to help with the nine-year patch

outcome.text: She tests you with one question about rot, decides you are not a fool, and puts you to work. You spend an afternoon thinning a fungal bed under instruction from a boar with better hands than yours. At the end she gives you a wrapped bundle and tells you what each one treats, twice, until you have it.

choices.text: She is doing something specific. Get down and look.

outcome.text:
The varaha does not stop or explain. She does move over slightly, which is permission.

What she is doing is grafting — one network into another, at a join she has prepared over what must be months. Nobody in the party had known this was a thing that could be done.

choices.text: Ask what the mycelium is connected to

outcome.text: She looks up for the first time. "Everything. That is the whole point." And she shows you: hands flat on the soil, the slow enormous conversation running under the entire forest, older than the trees standing in it, patient beyond any possible use. You take your hands off the ground eventually. She lets you sit with it for as long as you need.

animal_forest_sounder_matron.title: The Sounder Matron
animal_forest_sounder_matron.text:
She is enormous, grey around the snout, and lying in a wallow with the contentment of someone who has nothing left to prove to anybody. Two dozen varaha of assorted sizes are arranged around her in the mud.

One eye opens. "You are in my forest," she observes, without any particular concern about it.

choices.text: Apologise and withdraw

outcome.text: "Mm," she says, and closes the eye. The audience is over.

choices.text: Ask her the safe way through

outcome.text: She tells you, in detail, with landmarks, and includes which stretches are contested and by whom and at what hours. It is the single most useful conversation you have had since arriving in this realm.

choices.text: Sit down in the mud and stay a while

outcome.text: You get into the wallow. It is warm and appalling and after ten minutes you understand it completely. Nobody says anything for two hours. Piglets walk over you. When you finally rise, the matron says: "You may come back," which from a varaha of her standing is close to adoption.

choices.text: She is lying in a wallow, not guarding a pass. Approach accordingly.

outcome.text:
You come in downwind, slowly, at an angle, and you stop at the distance she chooses rather than the one you would prefer.

She lets you stop there. For a sounder matron with young in the trees behind her, this is an extraordinary concession, and both of you know it.

choices.text: You know exactly how this goes if it goes wrong.

outcome.text:
You have seen what a sounder does to something that got between the matron and the young, and the memory is specific enough to be useful.

You take the party the long way without arguing about it, and nobody finds out how it would have gone.

choices.text: Ask her advice on leading people

outcome.text: "Eat last," she says. "Sleep where they can see you. Never explain a decision twice — they stop believing the first one." She has run a sounder of forty for thirty years. You take notes, mentally, and use them for the rest of your life.

animal_forest_vanara_elder.title: Vanara Elder
animal_forest_vanara_elder.text:
The troop's elder holds court in the crown of a strangler fig, surrounded by an accumulated lifetime of stolen objects: brass buckles, a broken astrolabe, forty-odd single boots, a temple bell with no clapper.

"Sit," he says, indicating a branch. "Tell me something I don't know. Then you may have one thing."

choices.text: Decline the game politely

outcome.text: "Everyone's in a hurry," he says sadly, and goes back to sorting buckles.

choices.text: Tell him what you have seen in this realm

outcome.text: You describe the reef wall, the standing stones, the state of the northern trails. He listens with total attention and interrupts twice for detail. At the end he considers, then hands you a boot. Then, seeing your face, he laughs and gives you something better.

choices.text: Tell him something about his own troop he doesn't know

outcome.text: "Your second-youngest is not stealing food for herself. She has been running it up the east ridge every third day for a month." The elder goes completely still. Then he is gone through the canopy without a word, and comes back an hour later much older and much gentler, and gives you three things instead of one, and asks you not to mention it.

choices.text: Show him a sleight he has never seen

outcome.text: You palm his own tally-stick, produce it from behind a piglet's ear, and return it with the notches recut into a joke about him. The canopy comes apart with noise. He declares you troop-adjacent, grants you the freedom of every bridge in the forest, and immediately begins trying to learn the palm, badly.

animal_forest_high_canopy_perch.title: High Canopy Perch
animal_forest_high_canopy_perch.text:
A shyena is perched at the very top of the tallest tree in sight, motionless, looking out over the whole forest canopy. She has clearly been there for hours.

When she notices you at the base she does not startle. She simply looks down, once, and returns to looking out — which somehow communicates, precisely, that you are welcome to climb if you think you can.

choices.text: Leave her to her watch

outcome.text: She does not look down again.

choices.text: Call up and ask what she can see

outcome.text: "Everything," she calls back, unhelpfully. Then, relenting: the smoke to the north-east, the migration two days out, the gap in the ridge that the maps do not have. She gives it freely and goes back to watching.

choices.text: Climb up and join her

outcome_success.text: Forty minutes of climbing to sit beside something that got there in nine seconds. She says nothing about it, which is its own kind of courtesy. From up here the forest is not trees; it is one continuous green surface with weather moving over it, and you can see the ridge, the meadow, the sea. You stay until the light goes.

outcome_failure.text: You get two-thirds up before a branch you had committed to informs you it is dead. The fall is survivable, mostly because of the branches you hit on the way. From above, faintly, comes what is unmistakably laughter.

choices.text: Do not call up to it. Wait until it comes down.

outcome.text:
Everyone calls up. That is why the shyena is at the top of the tallest tree and not talking to anyone.

You sit at the base for two hours. It comes down in its own time, which is the only time it was ever going to come down in.

choices.text: Ask her what the sky-people make of the ground-people

outcome.text: "That you live in a tunnel and call it a world." She says it without cruelty — it is simply the view from up there. Then she describes the wind-roads: the thermals, the standing waves off the ridge, the column over the meadow that will lift a body a thousand feet if it is patient. You will never use them. You are glad to know they are there.

animal_forest_healer_camp.title: Healer's Camp
animal_forest_healer_camp.text:
Someone has strung a canvas between four trees and turned the space under it into a clinic. There is a queue: a gana with a bad leg, two vanara holding a third between them, a varaha piglet being extremely brave about something.

The healer — a gana, grey-muzzled, working fast — glances at your party and evidently sees nothing urgent. "Back of the line."

choices.text: Take your place in the queue

outcome.text: It takes two hours. When she gets to you she is thorough, blunt, and charges exactly what the work is worth.

choices.text: Leave the queue to those who need it

outcome.text: You go. Behind you the piglet is informed it has been very brave, which it clearly already knew.

choices.text: Roll up your sleeves and work the queue with her

outcome.text: She hands you the gana's leg without discussion and watches your first two minutes out of the corner of her eye. After that she stops watching. You work until the light goes. When the last patient limps off she treats your party for free, restocks your kit from hers, and says "come back" in a tone that means it.

choices.text: You know how to wait in a queue like this.

outcome.text:
You do, and you do it without complaining, which the healer notices from the other end of the line and files away.

When your turn comes she spends longer on you than the queue can really afford, and does not mention why.

choices.text: Somebody here is worse off. You have had worse than this.

outcome.text:
You give up your place, and then the next one, and by the end of the afternoon you have not been treated at all and have carried four people to the front of the line.

The healer finds you at dusk and treats you without being asked.

choices.text: Pay for the queue's treatment and move on

outcome.text: You settle the whole line's account and leave before anyone can make it into a moment. The healer catches you at the treeline anyway and presses herbs into your hand, scowling, as though you had done something inconvenient.

animal_forest_hedonist_camp.title: Hedonist's Camp
animal_forest_hedonist_camp.text:
Someone has been living extremely well out here. There is a fire, a great deal of fermented something in gourds, the remains of a genuinely impressive meal, and a shardula lying on his back in the middle of it all, utterly at peace.

"You look," he says, "like people who have been walking."

choices.text: Decline and keep walking

outcome.text: "Suit yourselves," he says, wounded on your behalf rather than his own, and pours another.

choices.text: Stay the night

outcome.text: It is a very good night. It is a considerably less good morning. You lose most of a day and some indeterminate amount of money, and the party is in a better mood than it has been in weeks.

choices.text: Match him gourd for gourd

outcome_success.text: At some point around the fourth gourd he stops treating it as a joke. At the sixth he concedes with enormous grace, declares you a person of substance, and gives you the good stuff — the sealed one he had not been intending to open for anybody.

outcome_failure.text: You do not remember the end of the contest. He does, and tells everyone in the forest about it for the next several years.

choices.text: You have opinions about this camp and you keep them to yourself.

outcome.text:
You decline everything — the gourd, the cushions, the extremely good food — politely and without comment, and your host finds this so novel that he follows you to the edge of the clearing asking questions.

He is, under all of it, lonely. You had guessed that from the size of the camp.

choices.text: He is pouring and you are not going anywhere.

outcome.text:
You are not. The evening is genuinely excellent and the following day is not, and somewhere in the middle you agreed to something you cannot reconstruct.

Your host, when you leave, looks briefly like someone watching a colleague go.

choices.text: He has more than drink out here and you can smell it.

outcome.text: He does. The two of you spend an hour agreeing about a number of things that will not survive contact with morning, and one thing that will: he tells you where the good stands are, and he is not wrong.

choices.text: Ask what he is drinking away
